items.title: Gene Bertoncini interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...you do some Eastman work? [INTERVIEWEE] Right. Eastman.

ctx.x: So there are people that can afford to pay a little more money to musicians but they always keep them on that servant level. And that’s a shame. But I think there is room for everybody. And follow your heart, follow your blisses, as Joseph Campbell said. And I just had breakfast, as I said, with my roommates, one of my roommates was a pianist in college. And he later went on to be, through the Marine Corps, a pilot for Delta Airlines. And he retired from Delta Airlines and he’s now a junior in college studying…
Well you speak very well of your philosophies about music and life too. I know you’ve been doing quite a bit of — you do some Eastman work?

Right. Eastman. The New England Conservatory. This year I’m teaching at William Paterson. I took Vic Juris’ place, because the king got too busy. I call him “the king.” He’s a monster. I love the way he plays. He’s working with the heavies too, David Liebman and Phil Woods and so, a monster player. So I’m honored to be there for him. And City College with Ron and occasionally Banff, and workshops whenever I can, I love that. I mean if my life was a bunch of what I did yesterday, a workshop and combined with a…
